title: My AI hero pipeline for a shipped mobile shooter: one concept image → TRELLIS-2 → a 6,000-triangle rigged character, about $0.38 each
author: sonnylazuardi
selftext:
GEMA is a 3v3 top-down tactical shooter that's live on the App Store and Google Play. The video is recorded on an iPhone. I built it with Claude Code, and five of the heroes are AI image-to-3D. Here's the pipeline, since that's the part I'd have wanted to read before starting.

**Per hero:**

1. Concept image: front A-pose on white, arms clear of the body, nothing in the hands. Nano Banana Pro, $0.03.

2. Image to 3D with TRELLIS-2 on fal, $0.35 a run. That gives about 480k triangles with 4K colour and roughness maps.

3. Try a few seeds and pick one from a contact sheet. Judge the back and the top of the head from the game's camera, because one front image can't specify them.

4. A script finds the joints on the mesh's own proportions: soles, knees, hips, shoulders, neck.

5. Reduce to two versions that share one UV layout: about 24,000 triangles for menus and about 6,000 for matches, with about 3x the detail on the head.

6. Bake the high-detail mesh's colour and normals onto the low one, bind it to the skeleton, and write it out as a module the game imports.

**What I learned:**

• The raw mesh is unusable on a phone. Nearly all the work is in steps 4 to 6.

• A-pose with clear arms matters more than the art style. Arms touching the torso fuse.

• Faces need the extra triangle budget or they turn to mush at match size.

**Not AI:** the map, lighting and effects are procedural code, and the rest of the cast is still procedural models.

It's free to try with no ads: [https://gema.sonnylab.com/?c=aigamedev](https://gema.sonnylab.com/?c=aigamedev)

Happy to share more detail on any step.
